Hi Olivia,

Thanks — this is clear and reasonable. Attached is a first-pass draft of exception language that treats customer-controlled infra as a shared-responsibility area and limits Redwood's uptime/latency guarantees to the Redwood-managed components and the runtime path inside the customer VPC when end-to-end network reachability is confirmed. Highlights:

- Redwood will commit to a 99.9% service availability for the Redwood inference runtime (process/service-level) for dedicated/private deployments, excluding outages caused by customer-controlled networking, on-prem hardware, or third-party transit.
- Latency SLOs (P95/P99) are stated as objective targets and are scoped to the runtime components; we will publish observed latency metrics to the customer telemetry endpoint within 5 minutes of ingestion.
- For incidents where customer network disruption is the primary root cause, Redwood will provide diagnostics and best-effort remediation guidance but cannot be held to uptime/latency SLA credits.
- We will include a technical annex describing required NAT/firewall rules, recommended MTU and keepalive settings, and required ports for KV/cache replication over the customer link.

I need internal confirmation on the specific uptime number and the telemetry delivery SLA. Markus and Jordan — can you review the attached draft and confirm whether 99.9% is the correct availability level for us to offer on Private (customer VPC) or whether we should push to 99.95% where we run a fully dedicated single-tenant cluster inside the VPC? Also confirm the 5-minute telemetry push is feasible.

I'll incorporate any edits and send a clean addendum for Sunridge procurement.

Best,

Subject: Fwd: RE: Private VPC — SLA expectations and carveout request

Lauren / Jordan — quick engineering read below (thread included for context). TL;DR: we can support a 99.95% availability commitment for a Dedicated single-tenant cluster deployed into a customer VPC, but only when the customer agrees to the network/HA requirements in the technical annex. Key points: 

- 99.95% is realistic if Sunridge deploys across two AZs (for multi-AZ failover) and provides low-latency backbone between hosts; otherwise 99.9% is the safe default.
- Network-induced latency spikes (packet loss, MTU mismatch, intermittent routing) are outside our control — those must remain carveouts.
- Telemetry: pushing aggregated metrics (availability markers, P95/P99 latencies, tail latency histograms) to Sunridge's monitoring endpoint at 1-min granularity is feasible; delivery within 5 minutes is acceptable for push + buffering. We should limit huge per-token traces to sampling for privacy/cost.
- For KV cache replication we need a paired node in the same AZ or low-latency cross-AZ link < 5ms median; call this out in the annex.

Suggested edit to the draft: offer 99.95% availability conditional on the customer meeting the annex requirements; otherwise 99.9% with documented compensation schedule. Also add a clause: "Redwood's SLA applies to the Redwood-managed software and runtime; Redwood does not warrant network connectivity, host hardware, or upstream transit provided by the customer."

If you're comfortable with this, I'll add the conditional language and the technical bullet list for the annex.

-Markus

Hi Olivia (and team),

Thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Attached is the revised SLA addendum and the technical annex. Summary of what we're proposing:

- Availability: Redwood will guarantee 99.95% availability for the Redwood-managed inference runtime when the following conditions are met: (a) Sunridge deploys across two AZs in the target region, (b) network RTT median between nodes is < 5ms cross-AZ and packet loss < 0.1%, and (c) the customer implements the annexed NAT/keepalive/firewall configuration.
- Carveouts: outages attributable to customer-controlled network configuration, on-prem hardware failures, ISP/transit interruptions, or changes to customer routing/policy are excluded from Redwood uptime/latency credits.
- Telemetry & logs: Redwood will push aggregated availability markers and latency metrics to the customer telemetry endpoint at 1-min granularity and guarantee delivery within 5 minutes of generation. Full request logs and sampled token traces will be available subject to agreed retention and privacy sampling.
- Remedy approach: where an incident is rooted in customer infra, Redwood will provide diagnostics and remediation guidance. Where the incident stems from Redwood-managed components, SLA credits follow the standard schedule in Section 4 of the addendum.

Next steps: I've attached the final PDF with redlines resolved. Please confirm procurement's preferred method (DocuSign or countersigned PDF). We can issue the addendum as an attachment to the master services agreement. If procurement wants any small language tweaks to the annex, loop us in — Markus is available for a short call to validate the technical checklist.
